method: Second review from supplied bytes, cleave facts, HTML parsing, Rizin control-flow and call-argument analysis, and inert mutation controls. No sample executed and no configured endpoint contacted. Scanner labels, scores, filenames, prior reports and external reputation were not used as verdict evidence.

samples.identification: Minimal news-digest HTML with repeated external script includes
evidence: Complete markup has two paragraphs, a news title, and 60 empty external script elements: 30 copies of each of two HTTPS URLs. Each element uses async and text/javascript. There is no inline script body, handler, hidden element, encoded payload, or additional local execution path.

In a browser, each eligible element loads and evaluates the remote response in the page context. Async affects scheduling and does not establish evasion. Repeated elements can execute a script repeatedly even when a response is cached.

Both previously hostile rules reduced to the same neutral remote-inclusion observation plus adjacency count and optional async. The matcher also convicts a head containing 60 different ordinary dependencies. It does not establish identical URLs, an unauthorized edit, a compromised site, or hostile response bytes.

The simple readable document, placeholder-style hosts and transparent inclusion mechanics favor a benign inclusion fixture or malformed page over a proven attack. The filename was not treated as evidence of injection. This is a likely-benign judgment, not a guarantee about unavailable remote responses.
samples.missing_context: Original package and page provenance, authorization/history of the includes, and the two remote script response bodies are unavailable. Injection, adware, exfiltration and C2 cannot be inferred from tag volume alone.
samples.changes: Retire two unsupported hostile composites and their unused Pinterest exception. Preserve notable remote-loading and adjacent-tag observations; ignore HTML comments when counting tag adjacency.

samples.identification: Urelas/MSMP native network and embedded-payload loader
evidence: PE32 entry 0x40c85b reaches CRT startup and WinMain at 0x401081. Its argument-sensitive installation path at 0x401955 reads concealed configuration, generates an executable name, copies its own image, launches the generated path at 0x402207 with the hi argument, and opens HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows at 0x402227. RegSetValueExW at 0x402250 writes that executable path as REG_SZ to Run. The Run pointer is resolved to VA 0x4215e0, not assumed to be adjacent to the key string.

Configuration reader 0x408b07 obtains a 512-byte block, complements its bytes at 0x408b59, and checks MSMP at 0x408b65. Paired writer 0x408b93 checks MSMP, complements a copied block at 0x408bd3, and saves it through 0x40888c. The complementary transform is actual code rather than an entropy inference.

Main calls 0x402655, which tries configured and embedded endpoints through 0x402719 and 0x40841e. Socket helper 0x404808 calls WSAStartup, socket, resolution and connect at 0x40497a. Protocol helpers use send/recv through their Winsock ordinal imports. Returned file information reaches 0x408656, which opens a path in the module directory with wb at 0x408827 and transfers received bytes through 0x404ee0. Main checks and launches the corresponding Temp7%X.exe path at 0x4011ff. This establishes remote bytes linked to a file-execution sink.

A separate path extracts resource 131 of type IDR_BINARY at 0x402974. Caller 0x402432 reconstructs a temporary executable through 0x402278 and launches it at 0x4025e6, then stores its event/state identifier as TrayKey. Do not confuse TrayKey with the separate Run persistence write.

Cleanup 0x403141 retrieves its own module path with GetModuleFileNameA at 0x403194. At 0x403236 it pushes that same stack-buffer address twice into the DEL/IF EXIST/GOTO format arguments. It writes the generated batch at 0x40325c and launches it hidden via ShellExecuteA at 0x40327b. This is linked self-deletion, not just co-occurrence of a delete template and a module-path import.

Raw-device paths reach CreateFileW and ReadFile. The record-recovery path at 0x403542 searches for _GBP records. No destructive disk overwrite was established. IsDebuggerPresent at 0x40c920 belongs to the CRT failure handler; its import alone is not an anti-analysis objective.

An encrypted ZIP member in resources was carved and decoded with password 1234: HanAgent_pe.exe, 228352 bytes, SHA-256 0742a171ff4693bb30cd153ca77039b1012b867ed7fa4aef30be00526ee55678. Its entry at 0x41207a uses an exception-based packed stub. The member was inspected statically; its complete unpacked behavior is not asserted.

Concealed loader state, remote payload activation, generated executable installation with logon persistence, and own-image deletion form a covert loader chain. These linked effects outweigh the ordinary GUI resources and the possibility that individual APIs serve legitimate software. The parent does not establish screenshot theft merely by naming HGDraw.dll.
samples.missing_context: Original registry package, operator authorization and deployment history are unavailable. No legitimate product/update workflow or user-facing explanation accompanies this loader. Family attribution is secondary to the directly traced behavior.
samples.changes: Retain the two supported hostile findings. Add a suspicious module-buffer-bound retry-delete formatter finding without family or artifact-name gates. Correct descriptions that assumed .rdata was read-only; rename uppercase RWX section observation to avoid inferring randomness. Remove the generic open/read/device-I/O group from the raw-disk tier, preserving the PhysicalDrive composite's required imports directly.

verification: Five HTML controls: exact repetition, renamed host, distinct dependency URLs, commented markup and a single include. All lack hostile/suspicious findings; the massed-tag observation applies only to the three executable high-volume cases.

Five PE controls: original and renamed batch preserve the self-delete finding; unrelated buffer, wrong API and wrong template pointer defeat it. All preserve the two independently supported hostile findings.
Six existing compromised-page regression fixtures pass after removing the two retired hostile IDs from expected results. Existing atob/eval and scam-funnel coverage remains tested.
